result.journal: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET)
result.keywords: The growing adoption of digital learning resources has prompted renewed interest in how university students evaluate print, electronic, and cloud-hosted textbook formats for academic study. This study examines students’ usage patterns, preferences, and acceptance intentions toward print and cloud-based e-textbooks in a private university in Southeast Asia. Using a survey of 248 undergraduate students enrolled in courses that offered both formats, the study applies descriptive and integrated acceptance analyses to compare perceived usefulness, content quality, pedagogical quality, social influence, and utility value across textbook formats. Findings suggest that students remain more comfortable with print textbooks for extended reading and focused revision, while cloud-based e-textbooks are favored for accessibility, portability, and convenience. Overall, respondents expressed positive attitudes toward cloud delivery but continued to prefer print as the primary medium for intensive academic study, with usage increasing when instructors explicitly required the resource.
result.title: University Students’ Acceptance of and Preferences for Print and Cloud-Based E-Textbooks
